To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LRP family is altered in the early stages schizophrenia.
LRP10 and APOE expression is altered in the early stages (first four years) of schizophrenia.

the mRNA expression of the low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 10 (LRP10) is increased and the mRNA expression of LRP12 is decreased, and apolipoprotein (ApoE) protein expression is increased, in schizophrenia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the apolipoprotein system in the pathology of psychiatric disorders and in particular schizophrenia.
the role of apolipoprotein signalling in schizophrenia, and we have recently identified several novel genes that are altered in the first 4 years of illness.
the identification of novel biological markers for the early stages of psychosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our findings support the hypothesis that aberrations in apolipoprotein signalling may play a role in the pathogenesis of schizophrenia.
LRP10 is increased and LRP12 is decreased in the prefrontal cortex of individuals with schizophrenia, which may be associated with the increased expression of APOE protein.

our results support a role for distinct LRP family members in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia and adds to the hypothesis that altered apolipoprotein expression is involved in the pathology of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LRP10 and APOE are increased in schizophrenia, whereas LRP12 is decreased in schizophrenia.
the early stage of schizophrenia is characterized by increased expression of APOE and LRP10, and decreased expression of LRP12.
LRP10, APOE and LRP12 may be involved in schizophrenia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown a novel role for LRP10 and APOE in the pathology of short duration of illness of schizophrenia.
the expression of several members of the LPR family of proteins are altered in subjects with schizophrenia and may play a role in the pathology of this disorder.
LRP10, LRP12, and APOE are potential biomarkers for the early stages of the disorder.
